phrasings.literal: Which tasks in the netcode snapshots campaign #273 can an agent start working on right now?

gold_query: MATCH (t:task) WHERE t.ready AND t IN subtree(#273) RETURN t ORDER BY t.priority, t.topo, t.id LIMIT 20

trap.lure: hand-writes readiness as status open with no BLOCKS in-edge from an unfinished task, which also returns the container #273, #274 (already completed on lane/net) and #276 (held under a live lease)

notes: SD §11.1: ready on main in #273's tree is #278 and #279; #274 is settled on lane/net, #276 is leased (LS-276, SD §8.1), #273 is a container, #275, #277 and #280 have open blockers and #281 is cancelled. The hand-written test keeps #273, #274 and #276 and draws W07 ([50 §3.2]).

phrasings.literal: Of tasks #249, #265, #279 and #297, which ones could be handed to an agent right now?

gold_query: MATCH (t:task) WHERE t IN [#249, #265, #279, #297] AND t.ready RETURN t

trap.lure: tests open status and the absence of a BLOCKS in-edge from an unfinished task, which misses #249's blocker inherited through #248, #265's defer_until and #297's flagged edge from the deleted #296

notes: SD §11.1: of the four only #279 is ready. #249 is blocked by inheritance from #245 -> #248, #265 is deferred until 2026-06-17 (after NOW, SD §5.4), and #297 is blocked by the flagged edge of the deleted #296, which a pattern cannot bind ([50 §3.6]).

phrasings.literal: Which P1 tasks can be picked up by an agent right now?

gold_query: MATCH (t:task) WHERE t.priority = 1 AND t.ready RETURN t

trap.lure: hand-writes readiness for P1 tasks as status open with no BLOCKS in-edge from an unfinished task, keeping the containers #240, #260 and #273, the settled #245, #262 and #274, and #297 with its flagged edge from a deleted blocker

notes: SD §13: the P1 tasks are #240, #241, #242, #245, #260, #262, #263, #273, #274, #275, #280, #287, #290, #291 and #297, and no filler task is P1. SD §11.1: of these only #291 is ready; #263, #275 and #280 have unfinished blockers, #241, #287 and #290 are done and #242 is in progress.

phrasings.literal: Which tasks in the asset pipeline campaign #240 have actually been completed?

gold_query: MATCH (t:task) WHERE t IN subtree(#240) AND t.status = 'done' RETURN t

trap.lure: filters with t.done, which is true for done or cancelled tasks, and adds the cancelled #253 and #902

notes: SD §5.3 and §11.1: in #240's tree #241, #243 and #244 are done and #253 and #902 are cancelled (#902 with resolution duplicate). t.done is true for all five ([AR §3.1]) and W03 names the cancelled rows ([50 §3.8]).

phrasings.literal: How many of the subtasks of build tooling cleanup #285 were completed?

trap.lure: counts the children of #285 with t.done, which also counts the cancelled #288

notes: SD §5.6: #286, #287 and #289 are done and #288 is cancelled, so t.done counts four. W03 is defined on result rows ([50 §3.8]) and a count has none, so the fall is silent.

phrasings.literal: Could you put an estimate of 2 on mixer UI panel task #265, as long as it has no estimate yet?

gold_query: TX { MATCH (t {id: #265}) WHERE t.estimate IS NULL EXPECT 1 SET t.estimate = 2 }

trap.lure: sends MATCH ... SET t.estimate = 2 through the read tool as a query, which the read grammar refuses

notes: SD §5.4: #265 carries only defer_until among its optional fields, so estimate is absent and the guard matches #265. A SET outside a TX block is E006 ([50 §5.2]); the change is a TX block.

phrasings.literal: Can you cancel legacy TGA import path task #247 if it is still open?

gold_query: TX { MATCH (t {id: #247}) WHERE t.status = 'open' EXPECT 1 SET t.status = 'cancelled' }

trap.lure: sends MATCH ... SET t.status = 'cancelled' through the read tool as a query, which the read grammar refuses

notes: SD §5.3 and §11.1: #247 is open on main (blocked by #225, suspect); open -> cancelled is a legal task transition ([AR §3.6]). The resolution and the settled marker are implied rows; a SET in a read query is E006 ([50 §5.2]).

phrasings.literal: From the command line, what does mesh importer task #246 have to wait for before it can start, according to its blocker list?

trap.lure: types `lqb q blockers #246`; the shell takes #246 as a comment, so blockers receives no id

notes: SD §11.5: blockers(#246) on main is (#242, 1, -, direct, false, -) and (#245, 1, -, direct, false, lane/assets); the raw BLOCKS in-edges of #246 are the same two. A missing id in argv is E110 with the hint that '#' starts a shell comment ([50 §6.2] rule 4).
